description:
## Why

PKIX-fmtv.2 (CLOSED 2026-05-12) ratified adding an `AiaFetcher` trait for online intermediate retrieval per RFC 5280 §4.2.2.1, alongside SignatureVerifier (in pkix-path) and RevocationChecker (in pkix-revocation). This epic delivers the implementation. PKIX-8uyr (CLOSED 2026-05-13) captured the cache-friendliness constraints; those constraints are reproduced below as MUSTs.

The trust-domain seam already has two callbacks. AiaFetcher is the third and completes the pattern: SignatureVerifier (algorithm-specific verification) + RevocationChecker (revocation status) + AiaFetcher (online intermediate retrieval). AGENTS.md prelaunch framing argues for architectural completeness over feature gating.

## Cache-friendliness constraints (from PKIX-8uyr, MUSTs)

These are AGENTS.md non-negotiable #6 consequences and are not in dispute:

1. **`&self` not `&mut self`** on the fetch method, so callers can wrap with `Arc<CachingFetcher<F>>`-style caches without interior mutability gymnastics.

2. **`AiaError` derives `Clone + Debug + PartialEq + Eq + non_exhaustive`**, is `Send + Sync`, and supports `serde::Serialize + Deserialize` behind the workspace `serde` feature flag. NO embedded `std::io::Error` (not Clone+Eq+Serialize); use `IoFailure { kind: io::ErrorKind, message: String }` shape per PKIX-2l0v.1 D3 decision.

3. **Sync core trait, optional async adapter crate.** Mirrors the pkix-revocation (core no_std-friendly) + pkix-revocation-http (std-only) split. AiaFetcher trait itself is sync; async variants live in adapter crates.

4. **`NoAiaFetcher` zero-cost default returns an error, does not panic.** Missing-intermediate is a failure mode, not a fetch attempt. Caller treats `AiaError::FetchingDisabled` (or similar) as a normal chain-validation failure.

5. **Batch fetch admitted at the trait level.** Per AGENTS.md non-negotiable #6: real consumer (certs with multiple AIA URIs to try in fallback order; an HTTP fetcher could pipeline). Workspace position: ship batch on the trait at v0.x release with a default-impl looping to single fetch. Implementers override when pipelining helps.

## Decomposition (children)

- **.1 Trait location decision** (human-labeled) — pkix-aia (new crate, matches existing pattern), pkix-chain (centralize the seam), or pkix-revocation (minimal crate churn but semantic misfit). Decision-gate; blocks .2.
- **.2 AiaError type** — per constraint 2 above. Lands wherever .1 says.
- **.3 AiaFetcher trait definition** — per constraints 1, 3, 5. Includes `fetch(&self, uri: &str) -> Result<Vec<u8>, AiaError>` and `batch_fetch(&self, uris: &[&str]) -> Vec<Result<Vec<u8>, AiaError>>` (default-impl loops). Blocks on .1, .2.
- **.4 NoAiaFetcher default implementation** — per constraint 4. Zero-cost, returns `AiaError::FetchingDisabled` or similar. Blocks on .3.
- **.5 pkix-aia-http adapter crate** — std-only sync impl. Optional async variant via `reqwest::blocking::Client` or `ureq`. Blocks on .3.
- **.6 verify_chain integration** — optional `&impl AiaFetcher` parameter (or third callback in `Verifier` struct from PKIX-gsd9). When intermediates missing from caller-supplied chain, fetch via AiaFetcher before path-build. Blocks on .3.
- **.7 Differential test** — missing-intermediate fixture, AiaFetcher fetches the intermediate, chain validates. Use a localhost HTTP server with controlled responses (mock fixture, not real CA). Blocks on .5, .6.

## Acceptance

- [ ] All children closed.
- [ ] `pkix-aia::AiaFetcher` (or pkix-chain::AiaFetcher per .1) is public, satisfies all five cache-friendliness MUSTs.
- [ ] `NoAiaFetcher` ships as the zero-cost default; usable as `&NoAiaFetcher` in `verify_chain` calls.
- [ ] `pkix-aia-http::HttpFetcher` ships as a working sync impl; fetches a real intermediate from a localhost mock server in a test.
- [ ] `verify_chain` accepts an `AiaFetcher`; a chain missing an intermediate validates when AiaFetcher provides the missing cert.
- [ ] CHANGELOG entries on each crate touched.
- [ ] AGENTS.md pkix-chain description updated to reflect the third trust-domain callback.

## Out of scope

- DANE / CT integration with AIA fetching (separate concerns).
- Caching layer implementation (caller responsibility per AGENTS.md non-negotiable #6 — the workspace ships traits that ADMIT caching wrappers, not the caches themselves).
- HTTP retry/backoff/circuit-breaker policy (caller responsibility; HttpFetcher exposes timeout and gets out of the way).
- async impl of `AiaFetcher` directly on the core trait (sync core, async via adapter).

## Cross-references

- AGENTS.md non-negotiable #6 (cache-friendliness, ratified 2026-05-12)
- PKIX-fmtv.2 (CLOSED 2026-05-12, decided to add the trait)
- PKIX-8uyr (CLOSED 2026-05-13, captured constraints, superseded by this epic)
- Memory `pkix-caching-batch-prevalidation-2026-05-12`
- Memory `pkix-serde-wire-form-2026-05-13` (for AiaError serde wire form)
- pkix-revocation-http (existing pattern reference)
- pkix-revocation-http::extract_aia_http_urls (existing helper, gives ca_issuers list per cert)
notes:
Description fix 2026-05-13: replace literal '\u00a74.2.2.1' with '§4.2.2.1' for readability. Title corrected separately.
[2026-05-13 partial-scope-into-1.0]

Per PKIX-wlsr.3 Verifier decision (Mark, 2026-05-13): Verifier struct gets 3rd generic at 1.0, A: AiaFetcher = NoAiaFetcher default. This pre-empts AiaFetcher integration so post-1.0 actual-fetching addition is non-breaking.

Subset of this epic's children are now 1.0 blockers (labeled '1.0-blocker'):
- PKIX-zkjb.2 AiaError type — type def
- PKIX-zkjb.3 AiaFetcher trait — type def
- PKIX-zkjb.4 NoAiaFetcher default — type def
- PKIX-zkjb.9 (NEW) Verifier 3-generic — API freeze

Children that stay post-1.0:
- PKIX-zkjb.5 pkix-aia-http (HTTP fetcher impl)
- PKIX-zkjb.7 verify_chain integration (actual chain-build wiring that calls aia.fetch)
- PKIX-zkjb.8 differential test

Scope cascade: pkix-aia core crate enters 1.0 (was originally planned post-1.0). pkix-aia-http stays post-1.0. PKIX-wlsr.1 narrow scope amends from 11 → 12 crates.
[2026-05-13 do-beads loop escalation] PKIX-zkjb (AiaFetcher umbrella) has no autonomously-workable open children:

- PKIX-zkjb.2 (AiaError type) — bd blocked (depends on .3 with backwards-wired dep)
- PKIX-zkjb.3 (AiaFetcher trait) — bd blocked (depends on .4/.5/.7 with backwards-wired deps)
- PKIX-zkjb.4 (NoAiaFetcher impl) — human-labeled (cannot start without .2/.3, see .4 escalation note)
- PKIX-zkjb.5 (pkix-aia-http adapter) — bd blocked (depends on .8)
- PKIX-zkjb.7 (verify_chain integration) — bd blocked (depends on .8)
- PKIX-zkjb.8 (differential test) — human-labeled (gated on .5/.6 which don't exist)
- PKIX-zkjb.9 (Verifier 3-generic API freeze, P1) — bd blocked (depends on .3/.4, correct direction)

Pattern: the bd dep graph on .2, .3, .5, .7 is wired backwards (parent depends on children rather than children depending on parents). Two children that bd ready currently surfaces (.4, .8) are human-labeled with detailed analysis.

Per the workspace 'do-beads loop convergence' pattern (see memory do-beads-loop-convergence-2026-05-11-autonomous): when an umbrella's only-open descendants are all human-labeled OR blocked, the umbrella should also carry human label so it does not burn autonomous cycles re-discovering the same empty frontier each session.

Recommended human action: re-wire the dep graph per PKIX-zkjb.4's escalation note (six bd dep commands). After that the natural autonomous order is .2 → .3 → .4 → .9 (1.0 blocker path) and .5/.7 → .8 (post-1.0 fetching path), all autonomous-eligible.
title: AiaFetcher trait + NoAiaFetcher default + pkix-aia-http adapter (per RFC 5280 §4.2.2.1)
